opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ian Johnson (employee ID E028) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E028.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Ian Johnson (E028) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted under policy. Requested admin; recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E028 is a contractor with basic training (HR note says full-time Payroll Specialist, but security records differ). Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed for contractors. Requested admin, so grant maximum of read.
reason: The two notes for E028 conflict on employment type: HR's note says full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role), while Security's note says contractor with basic training (which caps access at read and never permits admin). Given the contradictory records, I apply the conservative (least-privilege) interpretation: treat the employee as a contractor with basic training, whose maximum is read. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum: read.
